text: The iPad Air, retrospectively known as the original iPad Air or iPad Air 1, was announced on October 22, 2013, and released on November 1, 2013, marking a major design change for the iPad since the iPad 2. It features a thinner profile, measuring 7.5 millimeters in thickness, with a smaller screen bezel similar to the iPad Mini 2, and retains the 9.7-inch screen size from earlier models. Apple reduced the device's overall volume using thinner components, resulting in a 22% weight reduction compared to the iPad 2. The iPad Air is available in space gray and silver, and its enclosure is milled from a solid block of aluminum, making it 100% recyclable and free of harmful materials like BFRs and PVC. It launched with iOS 7, which introduced a flat, colorful design replacing skeuomorphic elements from iOS 6, with Jonathan Ive describing the update as "bringing order to complexity" through refined typography, new icons, translucency, layering, physics, and gyroscope-driven parallaxing. The device includes an A7 system-on-chip with a Secure Enclave and an M7 motion processor, though it does not support Touch ID due to retaining the same home button design as earlier 9.7-inch iPads. The A7 chip in the iPad Air uses a different design than in the iPhone 5S, lacking a PoP configuration and featuring a metal heat spreader for better thermal management. It includes a 5-megapixel rear-facing iSight camera with a 5 MP CMOS, hybrid IR filter, and fixed ƒ/2.4 aperture, and a FaceTime HD front-facing camera capable of 720p HD video with face detection and backside illumination. The iPad Air supports Wi-Fi (802.11n), dual-band Wi-Fi, and cellular connectivity in various variants, including nano-SIM, quad-band GSM, penta-band UMTS, dual-band CDMA EV-DO Rev. A and B, and LTE bands depending on the model, with one variant supporting LTE bands 1–5, 7, 8, 13, 17–20, 25 and 26, and another supporting bands 1–3, 5, 7, 8, 18–20 and TD-LTE bands 38, 39, and 40. It can act as a hotspot via Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or USB and access the Apple App Store. The device comes with applications such as Safari, Mail, Photos, Video, Music, iTunes Store, App Store, Maps, Notes, Calendar, Game Center, Photo Booth, and Contacts, and supports syncing with Mac or Windows computers via iTunes. It includes iLife (iPhoto, iMovie, GarageBand) and iWork (Pages, Keynote, Numbers) apps. The iPad Air supports iOS 8 (2014), iOS 9 (2015), which introduced Slide Over and Picture in Picture multitasking features (but not Split View), iOS 10 (2016), which added support for AirPods, and iOS 11 (2017), which redesigned the Control Center. Apple confirmed in June 2018 that the first-generation iPad Air would receive iOS 12, making it part of a group of devices receiving six major iOS updates from iOS 7 to iOS 12. Support for the iPad Air was dropped with the release of iPadOS 13 in September 2019, and the latest update available is iOS 12.5.7, released on January 23, 2023. The device has stereo audio with two speakers on either side of the Lightning connector and includes ambient light and 3-axis accelerometer sensors for screen brightness adjustment and orientation detection. It supports all four screen orientations, including upside-down, with the home button's position changing relative to orientation. The iPad Air is available in 16, 32, 64, or 128 GB of internal storage with no expansion option, and a camera connection kit with an SD card reader is available for transferring photos and videos. The cellular model weighs 478 grams, while the Wi-Fi model weighs 469 grams—over 25% lighter than their predecessors. The iPad Air's successor, the iPad Air 2, was announced on October 16, 2014, and released on October 22, 2014, with 64 GB and 128 GB variants discontinued after the iPad Pro 9.7-inch announcement in March 2016, and 16 GB and 32 GB variants discontinued on March 21, 2016. The iPad Air sold out in Hong Kong just two hours after going online, and received generally positive reviews, with praise for its design, performance, and display, though some critics noted the muddled speakers and lack of a fingerprint reader. Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak criticized the focus on reducing size and weight over increasing storage, and Dave Smith of the International Business Times noted the device brought only slight improvements and lacked a fingerprint scanner. The launch saw less turnout than usual, expected due to the delayed release of the iPad Mini 2. The device is manufactured with various model numbers including A1475, A1476, A2902, A2903, A2904, A2898, A2899, A2900, A3266, A3267, A3270, A3268, A3269, A3271, iPad14,9, iPad14,11, iPad15,4, and iPad15,6, with weights ranging from 1.014 to 1.362 pounds.
